Chronic stress activates the body’s stress response systems, including the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis, which results in elevated cortisol levels.  
Prolonged high cortisol can suppress immune function by reducing lymphocyte production and interfering with immune cell communication.  
This makes the body more vulnerable to infections and illnesses, which over time can damage health and reduce longevity.  

The other options describe possible indirect effects of stress in some individuals, but immune suppression is a well-documented direct physiological consequence of chronic stress.  

Final answer: (B)
